about.mission.title: Our Mission
about.mission.text: WorkChat Seattle’s mission is to help immigrant women across the greater Seattle area grow professionally, build careers, and realize their potential through learning, mentorship, meaningful connections, and mutual support.
about.values.title: Our Values
about.values.community.title: Community & Belonging
about.values.community.text: We foster meaningful connections and build a community where every woman feels welcome, respected, and valued.
about.values.support.title: Support
about.values.support.text: We understand the unique challenges women may face in their careers. We create a safe space for honest conversations, practical help, and mutual support.
about.values.growth.title: Growth
about.values.growth.text: We help women move toward their professional goals — whether they are looking for a job, changing careers, developing new skills, or advancing in their field.
about.values.empowerment.title: Empowerment
about.values.empowerment.text: We help women build the confidence, agency, influence, and leadership skills they need to shape their own professional paths.
about.values.learning.title: Continuous Learning
about.values.learning.text: We believe professional growth is an ongoing process. We encourage curiosity, knowledge-sharing, experimentation, and learning from both successes and setbacks.
about.story.title: Our Story
about.story.lead: The story of WorkChat Seattle began in the spring of 2018, when Masha Makarenkova, Masha Boone, and Guzel Gubeidullina organized a series of meetups for Russian-speaking women looking to build their careers in the U.S.
about.story.text:
What started as a small initiative grew into a community built on a simple belief: no woman should have to navigate her professional journey in a new country alone. From overcoming language and cultural barriers to rebuilding professional networks, we know how much difference the right connections and support can make.

Today, WorkChat Seattle brings together nearly 6,000 immigrant women from diverse professional backgrounds — tech and healthcare professionals, entrepreneurs, creatives, and many others. We host up to 20 events a year, from career workshops to AI study groups, while our members connect every day to share knowledge, job opportunities, referrals, and advice.
about.team.title: Our Team
about.team.text:
Join WorkChat Seattle team!
Every hour counts and every volunteer makes a significant difference.
about.team.masha.name: Masha Makarenkova
about.team.masha.bio:
Masha grew up in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, and has lived in several countries and U.S. states since finishing school. She holds a degree in Economics and an MBA from the University of Washington.

Masha has been involved in volunteer work since childhood. As a co-founder and Treasurer of WorkChat Seattle, she oversees budgeting and financial planning and makes sure resources are used efficiently. Her background brings a high level of expertise to our financial practices, and her experience is invaluable in navigating the financial challenges of nonprofit management.
about.team.tatyana.name: Tatyana Yakushev
about.team.tatyana.bio:
Tatyana Yakushev is a Principal Software Architect at Microsoft with more than 25 years of experience building software and leading engineering teams. Today, she develops AI-powered experiences in Microsoft’s Azure Data team, helping more people unlock the value of their data.

Through mentoring and workshops, she helps women build technical confidence and pursue ambitious careers. Tatyana believes that technology, combined with human kindness and a willingness to share knowledge, can help people grow and make the world around them better.
about.team.julia.name: Julia Seas
about.team.julia.bio:
Julia Seas is a product marketing and brand strategy professional with more than 20 years of experience. She helped build and scale marketing at 2GIS, one of Russia’s top 10 technology companies, and has led consulting projects for startups, small businesses, and nonprofit organizations.

Julia believes that women should not have to navigate their professional journeys alone. Together, they grow faster, advance their careers with greater confidence, and achieve more.
about.faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
about.faq.who.a: WorkChat Seattle is a community for women who have moved to the U.S. and are building, restarting, or growing their careers. Most members live in the greater Seattle area. You’re welcome at any career stage and in any field.
about.faq.join.q: How can I join WorkChat Seattle?
about.faq.join.a: The easiest way to join is through our Facebook group. Simply click the link above and request to join. We review requests regularly and will approve your membership shortly.
about.faq.russian.q: Do I need to speak Russian to join?
about.faq.russian.a: Most of our meetups and chat discussions are in Russian. It makes it easier to talk about complex things and understand each other without long explanations. Many of us speak other languages too, but Russian is the one we all share. That said, everyone who shares our experience is welcome. Some events are held in English, and the language of each event is always listed in its description.
about.faq.where.q: Where do your events take place?
about.faq.where.a: WorkChat Seattle hosts in-person events across the greater Seattle area, for example in Redmond and Bothell, as well as online workshops and webinars. The format, address, and language of each event are listed on its event page.
about.faq.free.q: Are the events free to attend?
about.faq.free.a: Most of our events are free. If an event has a fee, you’ll see it on the event page and when you register. Our community runs on volunteers and donations, so if you’d like to support our work, you can do it through the Donate button.
about.faq.updates.q: How can I stay updated about new events?
about.faq.updates.a: Subscribe to our newsletter at the bottom of our pages to hear about new events first. All upcoming events are also listed on our Events page and announced in our Facebook group.
about.faq.suggest.q: How can I suggest an event or speak at one?
about.faq.suggest.a: Use the “Suggest an event” button on our Events page to share an idea or an event you’d like us to know about. To give a talk or lead a workshop yourself, fill out the volunteer form and choose “Speaking or leading workshops.” We’ll review your request and get in touch by email.
about.faq.mentor.q: How can I become a mentor?
about.faq.mentor.a: We’d love to have you! Fill out the “Become a mentor at WorkChat Seattle” form on our Mentorship page and tell us about your experience, the topics you can help with, and your availability. You don’t need to have every answer. Relevant experience, a willingness to listen, and a wish to support someone’s growth are a great start. We’ll get in touch and, with your consent, publish your mentor profile so mentees can reach you directly.
about.faq.support.q: How can I support WorkChat Seattle?
about.faq.support.a: You can volunteer with our team, become a mentor, make a donation, or tell your friends about our events. If your company would like to partner with WorkChat Seattle or sponsor an event, email us at workchatseattle@gmail.com.
about.faq.nonprofit.a: Yes. WorkChat Seattle is a nonprofit corporation incorporated in Washington State and recognized by the IRS as a 501(c)(3) public charity. Donations are tax-deductible to the extent allowed by law.
about.faq.contact.q: How can I contact WorkChat Seattle?
about.faq.contact.a: Email us at workchatseattle@gmail.com. We’re happy to answer questions from members, mentors, speakers, and organizations interested in partnering with us.

home.testimonials.title: Our Stories
home.testimonials.kristina.title: WorkChat has had a huge impact on my career journey.
home.testimonials.kristina.text:
I first joined as a participant, then had the opportunity to help administer online meetings, masterminds, and book clubs.

Over the years, WorkChat's helped me pivot my career, prepare for interviews with major tech companies, and stay informed about what's happening in the corporate world.

This is an incredible network of like-minded professionals who genuinely want to help each other succeed. I'm so grateful to the founders, Masha Makarenkova and Masha Boone, for creating such a supportive community.
home.testimonials.kristina.name: Kristina E.
home.testimonials.natalia.title: This is the first and most active professional women’s group in our community.
home.testimonials.natalia.text: It’s been around since 2018, and I still remember how it all started. Now it is a place where you can get answers to any career-related question, find the most important information about different job roles, make the right connections, and meet genuinely bright, inspiring people. Thanks to WorkChat Seattle, I met not only amazing professionals, but friends I still cherish years later. I found a career coach I continue to work with, discovered my love for public speaking, got a lot of ideas and pivoted my career more than once, and always with this community behind me.
home.testimonials.natalia.name: Natalia B.
home.testimonials.yana.title: When I first relocated to Seattle to join Microsoft, this community helped me build both friendships and a professional network.
home.testimonials.yana.text: Through thoughtfully organized online and in-person events, I met amazing women, learned from industry experts, and stayed current on topics like AI, hiring trends, and career growth. I'm incredibly grateful to the organizers for creating such a welcoming and supportive space that has made Seattle feel like home.

mentorship.hero.title:
Accelerate your career
with guidance from women who've been there
mentorship.hero.text:
Explore career options, navigate your job search, or work through a workplace challenge with someone who can share relevant experience. Connect with a mentor through WorkChat Seattle or find other programs that fit your goals.

Mentorship is a conversation built on respect and a willingness to learn. You bring your questions and commitment to taking action, and your mentor shares her perspective and experience. While mentorship does not guarantee a job or promotion, it can help you make more informed decisions and approach your next step with greater confidence.

mentorship.faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
mentorship.faq.whoMentee.a: Any woman who is building, restarting, or growing her career in the U.S. You don’t need a perfect plan or a polished resume to reach out. If you have questions about your career, a mentor can help you sort through them. Our mentors speak Russian and English.
mentorship.faq.help.q: What can a mentor help me with?
mentorship.faq.help.a: A mentor is someone who has been where you want to go and is glad to share what they’ve learned. They can help you explore career options, understand how things work in U.S. workplaces, plan your job search, or think through a challenge at work. Depending on their experience, they may also give feedback on your resume, portfolio, interview preparation, or growth plans. Together you’ll choose a focus that fits your goals and their expertise.
mentorship.faq.free.a:
It depends on the mentor. Ask about their terms in your first message, so you both know what to expect from the start.

Other organizations’ programs listed on this page set their own fees and eligibility requirements. Check their websites for current details.
mentorship.faq.format.q: Is mentoring one-on-one or in a group?
mentorship.faq.format.a: Both are possible. Most mentoring is one-on-one, and some mentors also run group sessions, where you can learn from other women with similar goals too. Ask the mentor which format they offer.
mentorship.faq.online.q: Are meetings online or in person? What languages are available?
mentorship.faq.online.a:
Some mentors meet online, some in person, and some are happy to do either. Agree on what works for you both when you first get in touch.

Most of our mentors speak English and Russian, so you can talk about your career in whichever language feels more comfortable.
mentorship.faq.find.q: How do I find a mentor?
mentorship.faq.find.a: Browse the mentor profiles on this page. Each one shows the mentor’s background, the topics they can help with, and how to reach them on LinkedIn or by email. Pick someone whose experience speaks to your questions and write to them directly. It’s completely normal to reach out: our mentors joined because they want to hear from you. In your first message, tell the mentor a little about yourself: your background, what you’d like help with, and which language you prefer (English or Russian).
mentorship.faq.unavailable.q: What if the mentor I contact isn’t available?
mentorship.faq.unavailable.a: Please, don’t take it personally. Mentors are volunteers, and sometimes their schedule is full. Reach out to another mentor. If none of the profiles fits your questions, email us: we may know other people or programs that can help.
mentorship.faq.duration.q: How long does mentoring last, and how often will we meet?
mentorship.faq.duration.a: That’s up to you and your mentor. Some people meet once to get advice on one question, and others keep meeting for months. Agree on a schedule that works for both of you.
mentorship.faq.expected.q: What is expected of me as a mentee?
mentorship.faq.expected.a: Mentoring works best when you’re in the driver’s seat. Come with questions, prepare for meetings, and follow through on the steps you agree on. Be open to feedback, and let your mentor know if your goals or availability change. Your mentor brings perspective and support, and the decisions and the progress are yours.
mentorship.faq.job.q: Will my mentor help me get a job or provide a referral?
mentorship.faq.job.a: Your mentor can help you sharpen your job-search approach and feel more confident in interviews. Jobs, introductions, and referrals aren’t guaranteed or expected as part of mentoring, and mentors won’t fill out applications or rewrite documents for you. What you’ll get is someone in your corner who helps you move forward on your own.
mentorship.faq.becomeMentor.q: I want to share my experience. How can I become a mentor?
mentorship.faq.becomeMentor.a: We’d love to have you! Fill out the “Become a mentor at WorkChat Seattle” form on this page and tell us about your experience, the topics you can help with, and your availability. You don’t need to have every answer. Relevant experience, a willingness to listen, and a wish to support someone’s growth are a great start. We’ll get in touch and with your consent, we’ll publish your mentor profile on this page so mentees can reach you directly.
mentorship.faq.question.a: Email us at workchatseattle@gmail.com. We’re happy to help you understand the options and decide whether WorkChat mentorship fits your goals!

volunteer.hero.lead: Have valuable knowledge or expertise to share? Enjoy bringing people together? There are many ways to make a difference at WorkChat!
volunteer.hero.text:
More than 50 events. Nearly 6,000 community members. It all starts with people willing to share what they know and give a little of their time.
As a volunteer, you could help women feel welcome or find the courage to try something new. And as you become part of their story, they become part of yours — bringing new friendships, fresh perspectives, and a deep sense of belonging.
